question: Points $A$, $B$, $C$ have position vectors $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$, respectively. If $\vec{AB}$ and $\vec{AC}$ are adjacent sides of a triangle, find the area of the triangle in terms of $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$. If $\vec{b} = (2, 0, 1)$, $\vec{c} = (1, 3, -1)$, $\vec{a} = (0, -1, 2)$, compute the area numerically.
explanation:
The area of triangle $ABC$ with sides $\vec{AB}$ and $\vec{AC}$ is:

$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}| \vec{AB} \times \vec{AC} |$

$\vec{AB} = \vec{b} - \vec{a}$

$\vec{AC} = \vec{c} - \vec{a}$

$\vec{AB} = (2-0, 0 - (-1), 1-2) = (2, 1, -1)$

$\vec{AC} = (1-0, 3 - (-1), -1 - 2) = (1, 4, -3)$

Now, $\vec{AB} \times \vec{AC}$:

$\begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 & -3 \end{vmatrix}$

$= \hat{i}(1 \times -3 - (-1) \times 4) - \hat{j}(2 \times -3 - (-1) \times 1) + \hat{k}(2 \times 4 - 1 \times 1)$

$= \hat{i}(-3 + 4) - \hat{j}(-6 + 1) + \hat{k}(8 - 1)$

$= \hat{i}(1) - \hat{j}(-5) + \hat{k}(7)$

$= \hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$

Magnitude: $\sqrt{1^2 + 5^2 + 7^2} = \sqrt{1 + 25 + 49} = \sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}$

So, area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}$ units.
